transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-09-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Sofia Tran (CSM) — Anika Patel (Head of ML), Daniel Ruiz (Platform Eng), Leah Kim (PM), Rajesh Menon (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy): demo of eval console; discuss regression alerts; pilot; pricing.

00:00 Maya Chen: hi everyone thanks for jumping on, uh quick roundtable — can you confirm names + roles?
00:18 Anika Patel: hey yes this is Anika, Head of ML at Sunrise Health; Daniel, Leah and Rajesh are here too. thanks Maya.
00:23 Maya Chen: awesome, i'll do a 5-minute agenda: quick qual, then live console walk-through (prompt sets, alerting, A/B), then q&a and next steps. sound good?
00:34 Daniel Ruiz: yep that's good.
00:36 Maya Chen: cool. quick qualification — what are you running today for LLM inference?
00:42 Anika Patel: we currently proxy requests to a mix of OpenAI and a smaller self-hosted Llama variant for internal tasks. most production stuff runs through OpenAI due to latency and reliability.
00:52 Leah Kim: use cases: automated patient note summarization and triage assistant that surfaces follow up actions to nurses. latency target is ~400ms p95, cost pressure is real — we can't double our inference bill.
01:07 Rajesh Menon: security is the big blocker for any external vendor — SOC2, SSO, key management, and network controls (we prefer VPC peering or privateLink).
01:18 Luis Ortega: understood — we typically see these constraints. Redwood supports hosted and private deployments; Dedicated capacity or Private VPC can address the residency/peering ask.
01:27 Maya Chen: perfect. i'll hand off to Luis for the deep dive on the Eval console — he's going to demo prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons.
01:33 Luis Ortega: hey all. sharing my screen now — let me know if you can't see. (screen share noise)
01:40 [02:05] Luis Ortega: okay, in the console landing page you can see 'Evals' tab — sometimes our transcripts show it as EvalOps or Aperture, the UI label is Evals. starting with prompt sets: we upload a CSV of prompts + expected outputs + subjective rubrics. you can tag prompts by cohort (e.g., long encounter notes, short triage messages) and assign weights.
03:02 Anika Patel: can the prompt set include conversation history? some of our prompts are full threads.
03:08 Luis Ortega: yes — we support multi-turn prompts and chunking — the console will indicate sequence length distribution and recommend quantization / kernel profiles for performance. sometimes the UI mis-read K-V cache as K-V cash in transcripts, ignore that :)
03:35 Leah Kim: how do we handle golden outputs? we have subjective grading — not always a single ground truth.
03:42 Luis Ortega: great question — our Eval schema supports multiple references and pairwise comparisons. you can attach a rubric: correctness, hallucination, safety; each prompt can be scored automatically or with human-in-the-loop.
04:03 [04:30] Luis Ortega: next, regression alerts — you can create alert policies on metric deltas (e.g., average F1 drop > 3% over a window) or on distributional drift. alerts can be routed to Slack, email, or a webhook.
04:49 Rajesh Menon: are alert payloads PII-safe? we can't send PHI to external webhook endpoints.
04:56 Luis Ortega: by default we redact PII from alert snippets and you can configure the retention policy. for Private deployments, all alerting hooks can live inside your VPC.
05:12 Anika Patel: nice. can we test-run a regression on a subset or roll back to a previous model?
05:18 Luis Ortega: yep — in the console you can run ad-hoc evals against any saved model snapshot and do pairwise A/B comparisons. the A/B runner will compute pairwise win rates and show per-prompt diffs.
05:30 [06:02] Maya Chen: quick note on cost controls — the Eval runner supports batching and cost-estimation per-run so you can baseline expected tokens and GPU-hours.
06:15 Daniel Ruiz: how does this integrate with our current CI? we want nightly runs.
06:20 Luis Ortega: there is an API endpoint for eval runs — you can kick off a job via REST or SDK and get back a run_id, status updates, and result artifacts. we also have a lightweight CLI that plugs into CI.
06:32 Leah Kim: and streaming? some of our production uses streaming responses to the UI. can evals handle streaming metrics?
06:39 Luis Ortega: streaming is supported in production APIs; for evals we capture final outputs but we also capture latency traces and token-level timing so you can emulate real-time behavior.
06:55 [07:10] Anika Patel: what's the typical throughput for eval runs? if we have 10k prompts, how long?
07:16 Luis Ortega: depends on model, sequence length, and batch config — for an Llama-variant at 8-bit on a single A100 bucket you might get ~1k prompts/min with batching; our dedicated pools scale horizontally for bigger runs. we also provide estimated run time in the UI before you start.
07:43 [08:05] Maya Chen: interruption — competitors question — have you tried Anthropic or ModelServeX for similar workflows? what's your decision criteria?
08:13 Anika Patel: we've evaluated Anthropic in parallel but pricing and integration complexity were concerns. ModelServeX was on-prem but lacked the eval dashboards. key factors: security, easy prompts management, and reliable regressions alerts.
08:30 [08:52] Luis Ortega: noted. now switching to live A/B: i'm going to queue two model snapshots — model_v22 and model_v23 — run pairwise, show per-prompt diffs. initiating run... (spinner)
09:12 [09:58] Luis Ortega: run complete — here's the pairwise table: win-rate, tie-rate, average score delta. i'll open a prompt row so you can see the model outputs side-by-side.
10:05 Leah Kim: this side-by-side diff is great — can we export to csv for product analytics?
10:12 Luis Ortega: yes, export and an API endpoint returns the pairwise table as CSV or JSON.
10:18 [10:36] Rajesh Menon: are model artifacts signed? we need integrity proofing for audits.
10:43 Luis Ortega: we offer model versioning with signed manifests and hashes; for Private installs we can integrate with your HSM for signing.
10:51 [11:08] Maya Chen: ok moving on to regression alert tuning — you can set thresholds, time windows, and required sample sizes to reduce false positives. we also support bootstrap baselines so small traffic spikes don't fire alerts.
11:34 Anika Patel: we expect periodic concept drift as new meds and procedures come in. can we set cohort-level alerts?
11:41 Luis Ortega: absolutely — cohort level alerting is core: you can group by encounter type, region, or even clinician role tags.
11:51 [12:10] Daniel Ruiz: network question — what does Private deployment look like? VPC peering, private link?
12:17 Maya Chen: Private includes a customer-managed control plane and a pluggable data plane — options: VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an on-prem flavor. we can show a sample network diagram after.
12:34 Rajesh Menon: encryption at rest and KMS integration?
12:38 Sofia Tran: yes — KMS/HSM integration is available; we can support customer-managed keys and audit logs for every request.
12:45 [13:05] Anika Patel: curious about cost modeling when running evals frequently — any built-in amortization?
13:12 Luis Ortega: the Optimize toolkit suggests sampling rates, batching configs, and a cadence; you can schedule smoke runs nightly and full runs weekly. Optimize also suggests quantization profiles by prompting pattern — that reduces cost while preserving quality.
13:35 [13:58] Leah Kim: could you demo a regression alert being created end-to-end?
14:02 Luis Ortega: sure — creating alert: metric selection (e.g., hallucination rate), baseline window (last 14 days), threshold (delta 2.5%), notification channel (Slack #ai-alerts). I'll create a dummy alert now and trigger with a simulated run.
14:28 [15:00] Luis Ortega: ok alert fired — you can see the alert payload, suppressed snippets, and suggested rollback action (pin to previous snapshot).
15:15 Anika Patel: does rollback tie into our deployment pipeline or is it manual?
15:20 Luis Ortega: both — we integrate with deployment orchestrators so you can auto-roll back on severity or create an approval workflow.
15:30 [15:42] Daniel Ruiz: for the API, what auth schemes do you support?
15:47 Luis Ortega: API keys, OAuth with SSO/SAML, and mTLS for Private connections. role-based access control is configurable per-route and per-token.
15:58 [16:22] Rajesh Menon: audit logs retention policy? we need 13 months for compliance.
16:28 Sofia Tran: you can configure retention and export logs to your SIEM; for Private we can mirror logs to your S3 with lifecycle.
16:40 [17:05] Leah Kim: switching to prompts — can we version prompt templates and run backtests when we change them?
17:12 Luis Ortega: yes — prompt templates are first-class. every eval run records the exact template and tokens used; you can diff templates and backtest historically.
17:27 Anika Patel: if our prompts contain PHI, what's the recommended approach?
17:34 Luis Ortega: we recommend token anonymization or syntheticization in prompt sets for public dashboards; for private deployments, keep raw prompts in your VPC and use redaction only on external exports.
17:50 [18:05] Maya Chen: quick pause for questions from procurement/ops perspective.
18:10 Daniel Ruiz: billing — do you offer committed reserved capacity for lower unit costs?
18:15 Maya Chen: yes, that's Redwood Dedicated — committed GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower per-token costs; we can discuss tiers.
18:27 Anika Patel: what would a 3-month pilot look like?
18:30 Maya Chen: typical pilot: 4–8 weeks of integration + smoke evals, then a 6–8 week production-shadow pilot with defined success metrics. pricing is a small reserved bucket + usage overage. we'll send a proposed SOW.
18:48 [19:20] Rajesh Menon: i'd like to see SOC2 and any pen-test reports.
19:26 Sofia Tran: we'll share SOC2 summary and our latest security pack; if needed we can arrange an NDA for any additional docs.
19:35 [20:00] Luis Ortega: switching back to the console — i'll show an alert trends dashboard and the ability to group alerts by severity. you can also link alert hits to a ticketing system.
20:18 [20:52] Leah Kim: is there a way to auto-sample false positives for human review?
20:58 Luis Ortega: yes — you can attach a human-review workflow and send random samples to a review queue; results feed back into the training set.
21:12 Anika Patel: how does the A/B runner handle significance testing?
21:18 Luis Ortega: we compute bootstrap confidence intervals and provide p-values for selected metrics; for pairwise comparisons we show statistically significant wins at configurable alpha.
21:37 [22:00] Daniel Ruiz: perf question: what's p95 latency impact when eval runner runs heavy jobs?
22:08 Luis Ortega: evals run on separate batch infrastructure by default so they don't affect online serving; if you run evals against the same Dedicated pool we can schedule low-priority background jobs to avoid interference.
22:28 Maya Chen: ok, quick demo endpoint — I'll show the SDK call to kick off an eval. (short code paste)
22:40 [23:05] Maya Chen: code snippet: redwood.evals.run({prompt_set_id, model_snapshot, webhook}) — returns run_id. you can poll status or subscribe to webhooks.
23:20 Leah Kim: can we parameterize prompt templates per-clinic or per-user?
23:26 Luis Ortega: yes — templates accept variables and you can store per-tenant overrides.
23:33 [24:00] Anika Patel: operational question: do you keep historical outputs for debugging?
24:07 Luis Ortega: by default we retain runs for 90 days but retention is configurable and exportable. sensitive data can be encrypted with your KMS and stored in your bucket for longer.
24:22 [24:50] Rajesh Menon: any examples of customers using this for healthcare?
24:56 Maya Chen: we have a couple of health-tech customers running note-summarization and prior-auth automation — we can share anonymized case studies.
25:10 [25:40] Leah Kim: could you show how to construct a regression alert tied to a prompt cohort?
25:46 Luis Ortega: creating cohort: filter by tag 'triage-short', build metric 'avg hallucination', baseline window 30 days, threshold 3%, action: webhook to internal webhook — done. i'll show simulated hits.
26:10 [26:42] Luis Ortega: alert details include trending charts, sample outputs, and suggested remediation like 'reduce temperature' or 'fallback to pedigree model'.
26:58 Anika Patel: fallback policies — can we have auto-fallback to a smaller cheaper model during peak?
27:04 Luis Ortega: yes — smart routing policies allow cost tier routing and fallback chains; you can route by latency budget or cost budget.
27:20 [27:45] Daniel Ruiz: question on token accounting — do logs break down per-prompt token usage?
27:52 Luis Ortega: yes — per-request token breakdown by prompt and completion tokens, cost per token surfaced on the run artifact.
28:08 [28:30] Maya Chen: small note: sometimes the transcripter writes Redwood as RedWood or Red wood — irrelevant but FYI.
28:36 [29:05] Leah Kim: can we run A/B on non-deterministic models and get stable stats?
29:12 Luis Ortega: we seed runs, record random seeds, and run multiple samples per prompt to stabilize estimates; we show confidence intervals accordingly.
29:30 [30:00] Sofia Tran: security interjection — for Private we can host the control plane or provide a hybrid model; we'll put options in the doc.
30:15 [30:42] Maya Chen: demo wrap-up — quick recap of features shown: prompt sets with rubrics, pairwise A/B runner, regression alerts, cohort-level monitors, API + CI integration, and private deployment options.
30:58 [31:20] Anika Patel: this is helpful — timeline wise, we need to present to procurement and legal by 2026-09-11.
31:27 Maya Chen: great — we'll aim to get security pack and pricing this week.
31:34 [31:55] Leah Kim: one more: do you support custom metrics plug-ins (we compute clinical-accuracy metric)?
31:59 Luis Ortega: yes — you can upload custom metric functions (sandboxed) or run a hook that computes metrics offline and import results into the dashboard.
32:15 [32:48] Daniel Ruiz: what about drift detection for embeddings? we use embeddings for retrieval-augmented tasks.
32:55 Luis Ortega: embeddings drift is supported — cosine distribution monitoring, nearest neighbor stability, and alerting on vector-space shifts.
33:12 [33:40] Rajesh Menon: last security Q: vulnerability disclosure and incident process?
33:46 Sofia Tran: we have an incident response playbook and a responsible disclosure contact; we'll include contacts in the security pack.
33:58 [34:20] Maya Chen: ok, time for a brief recap and next steps.
34:27 Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to send pilot pricing + SOW, share eval runbook + sample dashboards, security docs; Customer to provide prompts + rubric and confirm pilot timeline; schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-09-13.
34:46 Anika Patel: sounds good.
34:49 [35:10] Maya Chen: any final questions?
35:15 Leah Kim: none from me.
35:17 Daniel Ruiz: thumbs up.
35:19 Rajesh Menon: will review security docs.
35:22 Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone; we'll follow up over email and post the deck and artifacts.
35:30 [END transcript — some timestamp noise and imperfect speaker labels expected from auto-transcribe]
